clue.text: Relations with God forced doctor to have settled in low ground from loftier place?

parts.note: kin are one's relations

indicators.note: forced suggests the letters of God are pushed out of shape into a new order

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: in has the rearranged letters lodged inside the word for low ground

parts.note: a fen is low marshy ground, as in the English Fens

indicators.note: settled hints that the letters of have are resettled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A family's dealings with God involve a doctor forced to settle down in the lowlands from somewhere higher up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' turns GOD into GDO; 'settled' turns HAVE into HEAV, which goes 'in' FEN to give FHEAVEN. The question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven, God's realm in the Gospels, is conventionally thought of as above us, a loftier place than earth.

clue.text: Saw, with thanks, Warrant Officer Turner is savvy

indicators.note: a turner is one who turns, so the word signals the letters before it being turned about into a new order

parts.note: WO is the military abbreviation for Warrant Officer

explanation.surface: A Warrant Officer named Turner, thanked for his saw, proves himself shrewd.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the officer's surname (or the painter) but is the anagram signal working on SAW WITH THANKS WO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone savvy is shrewd and well informed, which is exactly what the idiom about knowing the true state of affairs conveys.

clue.text: Relation heard to be in the south of France

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: Nice is a city on the Riviera in southern France

explanation.surface: A family member is reported to be on holiday on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is one kind of family relation.

clue.text: Chinatown needs reform to follow doctor

indicators.note: to follow places the reworked letters after the doctor's abbreviation
reform asks for the letters of needs to be formed again in another order

explanation.surface: A Chinatown district needs regeneration and should take its lead from a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Chinatown' as 'china town': the German city famous for its porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saxon city gave its name to a celebrated porcelain, so it is a town known for china.

clue.text: Setter holds a sticker for early show

indicators.note: holds means the setter's pronoun contains the other pieces

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
a tine is a prong, something that sticks into things

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is holding a sticker for an afternoon performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often call themselves ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance, earlier than the usual evening show.

clue.text: Old dreamer found infant a study

indicators.note: found signals that the answer is discovered lying inside the run of words infant a study

explanation.surface: An elderly visionary discovered a baby being studied.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantast is a visionary or dreamer; the word is now old-fashioned, hence old.

clue.text: Gospel walker with a lot of church backing

indicators.note: backing indicates the combined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: a leg is what one walks with
the nave is the main body, the largest part, of a church

explanation.surface: A gospel-singing pedestrian enjoys much support from the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LEGNAVE round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an old word for the gospel, the good news preached by the evangelists.

clue.text: Such are fuses to light rainbow, many the work of suckers

parts.note: lighting circuits use five-amp fuses, written with Roman V for five followed by amp
Iris was the Greek goddess of the rainbow, and iris means rainbow
M, Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Fuses blown by light, a rainbow, many strange things that bloodsucking creatures might do.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British home the lighting circuit is protected by a 5-amp fuse: V (Roman five) plus AMP.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloodsucking of vampires is literally the work of suckers.

clue.text: Eventual result, including gift, that's computed about future operation

indicators.note: including puts the gift inside the rearranged letters
result suggests the letters of Eventual are produced again in a new order

parts.note: a present is a gift

explanation.surface: The final outcome, gift included, is what an accountant works out about a planned project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' is the anagram signal and 'including' the container; 'Eventual' looks like an adjective on 'result' but is the fodder, giving NETVALUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Accountants calculate this discounted cash-flow figure to judge whether a future project will pay.

clue.text: Been greedy about school, say

indicators.note: say indicates the words are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: over means about, as in a dispute over something, and Eton is the famous public school

explanation.surface: Someone has been greedy about a school, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known public (private) school.
explanation.definitionFit: To have eaten too much is to have been greedy at the table.

clue.text: Let in to make confession

definitions.meaning: allow entry, as a doorman does

explanation.definitionFit: To admit is both to allow entry and to acknowledge a fault.

clue.text: Financier of Oxford theatre occupied in issue

indicators.note: in places the word for occupied inside the word for issue

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
held means occupied, as a post or a seat is held

explanation.surface: The backer of a university theatre was caught up in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Archbishop Gilbert Sheldon paid for Wren's Sheldonian Theatre in Oxford. 'issue' means offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Archbishop Gilbert Sheldon met the cost of building Oxford's Sheldonian Theatre, which bears his name.

clue.text: Heart of Hilton's 1 across gets Queen in worse temper

indicators.note: heart of keeps only the inner letters of the paradise, dropping two letters from each end

parts.note: in James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon the earthly paradise is Shangri-La
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The centre of a Hilton hotel's paradise sees a queen getting crosser.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilton is the novelist James Hilton, not the hotel chain. 'Heart of' drops SH and LA to leave ANGRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Angrier is the comparative of angry, describing someone in a worse temper.

clue.text: See 16
Each way round enclosure makes little money

indicators.note: round puts the rearranged letters around the enclosure
way here suggests the letters of Each are taken a different way, rearranged

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: An each-way bet placed around the paddock earns only a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: An each-way bet is a racing wager on a horse to win or place; here 'way' signals the anagram (HACE) and 'round' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Ha'pence were halfpennies, the smallest British coins, so a trifling sum.

clue.text: All but the subject spread around: drink up!

indicators.note: around puts the spread outside the other piece

parts.note: pate is a spread for toast

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: Everything except the main topic is laid out: bottoms up!
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses, giving REDIC; 'spread' looks like a verb but is the food paste, and 'drink up!' poses as a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a sentence's predicate is everything in it except the subject.

clue.text: Flower and golfer are beasts

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Cam flows through Cambridge
Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: A bloom and a golf player turn out to be animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword river: that which flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Dromedaries and Bactrians are large desert beasts of burden.

clue.text: Jethro, first American with Cicero's name

parts.note: Jethro Tull was the agricultural pioneer who gave his name to a rock band
I is one, the first

explanation.surface: Jethro Tull, the first American to bear the orator Cicero's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The orator's full name was Marcus Tullius Cicero, so this is his family name.

clue.text: Ulster's first to get itself higher education

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Ulster's

parts.note: Ulster itself, the province, is Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: The leading figure in Ulster gets to go to university himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is often used as a name for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British shortening for university, the main place of higher education.

clue.text: Beat around railway with tax avoidance scheme

indicators.note: around has the word for beat surround the railway

parts.note: to thump is to beat
EL is the elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: Thrashing around the railway with a scam to dodge taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the lump' was building labour paid as self-employed lump sums to avoid tax and national insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a British construction-industry practice of paying casual workers cash lump sums, avoiding income tax deductions.

clue.text: Have dubious fun with heartless country in appropriate style

indicators.note: dubious suggests fun is of doubtful form, so its letters are reshaped
heartless removes the central letter of the country

parts.note: Italy is a European country

explanation.surface: Have some shady amusement in a heartless land in the right manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition must be read as 'in-appropriate style', i.e. inappropriately; bloggers disputed this. 'heartless' drops the middle A of ITALY to give ITLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfitly means in an unsuitable manner, which is what in-appropriate style comes to.

clue.text: Architectural promoter to lead round a ring

indicators.note: round puts the word for lead around the article a

parts.note: a plumb is a lead weight on a line
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: To guide someone around a circus ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord (Peter) Palumbo is a British property developer and patron of architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Palumbo, developer and chairman of architecture's Pritzker Prize jury, is a noted champion of modern architecture.

clue.text: Dives into 1 across with more difficulty than 16 13 through 30

definitions.text: Dives into 1 across with more difficulty than 16 13 through 30

parts.words: Dives into 1 across with more difficulty than 16 13 through 30
parts.note: Jesus said it is easier for a desert beast to pass through a tiny hole than for a wealthy person to enter God's kingdom; Dives is the Vulgate's word for the wealthy man in the Lazarus parable

explanation.walkthrough: Dives is not a verb but the Latin name given to the wealthy man in the parable of Lazarus.
explanation.definitionFit: Dives, Latin for wealthy, is the traditional name for the wealthy man in Luke's parable.

clue.text: 11's theatre, say, with rubbish below, say

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: the second say asks for the word as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: under means below

explanation.surface: An Oxford theatre, for example, with garbage underneath it, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic British accent, where 'under' ends like UNDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sheldonian is a round building, an example of a domed circular hall.

clue.text: Hiding place in which to put the French carriage

indicators.note: in which to put means the French article goes inside the hiding place

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A secret hideaway in which to keep the French coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A light horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood, also spelt calash.

clue.text: Trouble the year before our epoch?

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels years of the present era
a year zero would come just before year one of the era, written 0

explanation.surface: Problems in the year before our era began?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits there was no year 0: AD 1 followed 1 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss and bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: What's wrong about monarch? Too much liquor?

indicators.note: about puts the word for wrong around the monarch

parts.note: sinful means morally wrong
K stands for king, a monarch

explanation.surface: Is there anything wicked about the king? Has he drunk too much?
explanation.definitionFit: A skinful is an informal British term for as much alcohol as one can hold.

clue.text: Exam permitted with backing capital

indicators.note: backing means the joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination
let means permitted

explanation.surface: An exam is allowed, with financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns VIVALET round as a whole. 'capital' looks financial but is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is often cited as a capital city, since many countries keep their embassies there.

clue.text: See about a quiet flat

indicators.note: about wraps the word for see around the other pieces

parts.note: vid, short for vide, means see in references
p, piano, means quiet in music

explanation.surface: Look around a peaceful apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat and insipid are synonyms for something lacking interest or flavour.

clue.text: Middleman taking pictures

parts.note: he refers to a man
pictures as a whole are art

explanation.surface: An agent who takes photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middleman' must be split: 'Middle' defines and 'man' gives HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its centre or middle.

clue.text: Most of German city has one friend relating to it

indicators.note: most of drops the last letter of the city

parts.note: Munich is the Bavarian capital
I is the Roman numeral one
pal means friend

explanation.surface: A German city has one ally of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the city: the answer means relating to a city or town.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal means relating to a town or city and its local government.

clue.text: Little space for Spooner's image's bender

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of words, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: the knee is what bends
an idol is an image of a god

explanation.surface: Very little room for a statue's knee joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'image's bender' is 'knee of an idol'; swapping the opening sounds gives the phrase. Bloggers note it is a vocalic, not consonantal, Spoonerism.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny hole in a sewing needle stands for an extremely small space.
